text: "Gake no Ue no Ponyo" (崖の上のポニョ; "Ponyo on the Cliff") is the theme song to the Studio Ghibli film Ponyo, released on December 5, 2007, though it gained widespread popularity with the film's release in August 2008. The song was performed by folk group Fujioka Fujimaki and eight-year-old Nozomi Ōhashi. It was written in collaboration between veteran Ghibli composer Joe Hisaishi, with lyrics by film supervisor Katsuya Kondō and director Hayao Miyazaki. When Hisaishi first saw the storyboards, he immediately composed the melody but considered it too simple and did not share it for two to three months before showing it to Miyazaki and producer Toshio Suzuki, who both felt the simple melody was appropriate for the film. In addition to being featured in the film and commercials, the song was used in advertisements for Mitsuya Cider. Fujioka Fujimaki and Nozomi Ōhashi performed the song on the Kōhaku Uta Gassen new year's song contest, making Ōhashi the youngest participant in the show's 59-year history. The song was a major success on Oricon's physical single charts, initially charting at #115 for one week after its December 2007 release, then re-entering below the 100 mark in early July, breaking into the top ten at #6 by the end of July, spending 11 weeks in the top 10 with a peak of #3 for four weeks, and remaining in the top 50 for 15 additional weeks—entering the top 20 around New Year's due to Kōhaku Uta Gassen—before dropping out of the top 200 in August 2009, having spent over a year on the charts. On the Billboard Japan Hot 100 (combining physical sales and airplay), the song peaked at #4 and was the 17th most successful song of 2008. Digitally, it reached #1 on RIAJ's monthly ringtone chart and has been certified platinum for full-length cellphone downloads and double-platinum for ringtone downloads. For the overseas release of the film, an English version retitled "Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea" was released, sung by Noah Cyrus and Frankie Jonas (siblings of Miley Cyrus and the Jonas Brothers), and released as a digital download in May 2010, despite the film's North American release in August 2009. Two versions of this cover were created: one a direct stylistic cover of the original and another an upbeat pop rock remix.
